newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SPEED SKATING-DUTCH CLEAN UP AT EURO CHAMPIONSHIPS.
newsitem.headline: SPEED SKATING-DUTCH CLEAN UP AT EURO CHAMPIONSHIPS.

text.p: Dutch speed skaters achieved a virtual clean sweep at the European Championships on Sunday, taking all three top men's positions and two of the three in the women's competition.

Friesian Ids Postma took gold in the men's event with a points tally of 157,790, beating fellow Dutchman Rintje Risma, European champion for the last three years, into second place. Falko Zandstra, also of the Netherlands, was third.
Postma, who becomes the 17th Dutchman to take the European title, won the 500 and 1,500 metres. He was second in the 5,000 and third in the 10,000 metre distances.

In the women's competition, Tonny de Jong of the Netherlands took gold, with Germany's Gunda Niemann silver and Dutchwoman Barbara de Loor bronze. De Jong won with a points total of 169,375 -- a new Dutch national record.
De Jong won three distances -- the 1,500, 3,000 and 5,000 metres, coming second in the other, the 500 metres. It was the 22-year-old's first international title.
The last Dutchwoman to win at the European championships was Atje Keulen-Deelstra in 1974.
